source.title: Placement Is Free, Composition Is Not: The Latin Square as a Provably-Balanced Construction for Heterogeneous Sequence-Mixer Stacks
source.authors: Taebong Kim; Youn-Sik Hong; Minsik Kim; Sunyoung Choi; Jaewon Jang; Minseo Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study uses controlled, parameter-matched architecture ablations to measure how mixer arrangement and composition affect held-out cross-entropy; it does not reproduce a scaling-law fit.
record.gate_note: The ablations test V4 by comparing held-out cross-entropy across parameter-matched mixer arrangements and compositions. The paper does not fit or test power laws, predict larger-run losses from smaller runs, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its benchmark and Korean word-order results do not test downstream predictability with scale or pretraining loss. Per-mechanism latency and memory measurements are not loss results.
record.test_reason: The study's placement arms hold parameters (700.9M) and the mechanism multiset fixed and vary only the depth arrangement. Held-out cross-entropy is reported for each arm, so the results bear on V4 in a new setting: hybrid sequence-mixer stacks. The study is not aimed at scaling laws. The composition arms change which mixer types are present, which is a change of architecture family rather than a shape detail, so they do not bear on V4. No power-law fits, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or scale-to-downstream relation is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that within distributed schedules the exact permutation is free (Latin ≈ periodic). Confining mechanisms to depth bands costs 0.59% and homogenizing costs 1.68%. The composition benefit is carried almost entirely by the SSM-family mechanism, and the attention variants are interchangeable at this scale. The composition penalties persist and grow at 1.514B, while placement was not re-tested at that scale. They argue the Latin square is a principled, search-free default for delivering distributed balance.
record.recipe_differences: The study conducts parameter-matched mixer-placement and composition ablations rather than fitting scaling laws or estimating compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on mixer composition and depth distribution: the attention-variant removals are within noise, whereas removing Mamba-2, clustering mechanisms, or using a homogeneous stack raises loss. Placement arms were not repeated at 1.514B.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed parameter count, changing which sequence-mixer types are in the stack changes loss by different amounts. Collapsing to homogeneous full attention adds 1.68% at 700.9M and 2.63% at 1.514B. Removing Mamba-2 adds 2.14% and 3.20%. Removing any single attention variant is within noise (≤0.18%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed parameter count, mixing state-space and attention mixers lowers loss relative to homogeneous or SSM-free stacks, and the gap widens with model size.

record.problems: The ablation is a proxy with four mechanisms and sixteen layers, trained for 1,500 steps; it is not the 6.59B flagship configuration. The placement axis was not tested at 1.514B, neither axis was tested at flagship scale, and the larger-scale table gives means without uncertainty values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. Benchmark scores and Korean word-order perplexities do not test the listed scaling or downstream-predictability versions.

untested.parts: All of it. There are no loss-versus-parameters, tokens or compute power-law fits. Two model sizes are compared at a fixed 1,500 steps.
All of it. No fit-and-extrapolate test is done.
All of it. No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is studied.

Depth and width sweeps within the wide range V4 names. Placement effects at 1.514B or at flagship scale. Placement effects at a longer training length than 1,500 steps (losses around 5.3 are far from converged).
All of it. Only text pretraining is studied.
All of it. Benchmarks are reported only for the single flagship model, with no relation to scale or loss.
All of it. No fitting choices or exponents are examined.

record.verdict_notes: This is a weak, indirect bearing on V4. The paper is about hybrid-mixer design, not scaling laws. The proxy is trained for only 1,500 steps (loss ≈5.3), so any generality of these small differences is uncertain. The reader's limits_scope label rested on treating statistical significance as contradicting 'only slightly'. Effects under 1% fit V4, and mechanism-set changes are outside V4. The 1.514B table gives no seed-level uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law behavior in parameters, tokens, or compute over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.

Tests mixer arrangements and compositions in a four-mechanism, 16-layer proxy, not broad depth, width, or other architecture sweeps. The placement arms are not repeated at 1.514B parameters, and neither axis is tested at flagship scale.
Other modalities, repeated-data scaling-law tests, fine-tuning, and transfer scaling laws.
No relationship between downstream performance and model scale or pretraining loss is tested.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices or fitted exponents.

relationships.condition: Rearranging the same four-mechanism multiset across depth in a 700.9M parameter-matched proxy at 1,500 steps (Latin vs. periodic vs. block)
relationships.reason: Periodic differs from Latin by +0.16% (null), and even confining each mechanism to a depth band costs only +0.59%. Both are slight changes at fixed parameter count; see R1–R3.
relationships.display_finding: Periodic placement increased loss by 0.16% relative to Latin placement, while grouping each mechanism into a depth band increased it by 0.59%.

tranche.reason: Parameter-matched heterogeneous sequence-mixer stacks provide a new setting testing V4 through held-out cross-entropy under different depth arrangements.

source_check.notes: Placement results cover the 700.9M proxy at 1,500 steps and sequence length 1,024; placement was not retested at 1.514B or flagship scale. R2's observed state refers to V4's slight sensitivity to architecture, consistent with a null placement difference.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Distributed periodic schedule and leave-one-out removal of the three attention variants in the 700.9M proxy
reader_labels.reason: The periodic schedule differs from the Latin reference by +0.16%, and removing sliding, differential, or full attention is reported as within noise; see R2 and R5–R7.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Block and homogeneous arrangements, and removal of the SSM-family mechanism in the 700.9M proxy; composition checks at 1.514B
reader_labels.reason: Loss increases are measurable for block placement (+0.59%), a homogeneous stack (+1.68%), and removal of Mamba-2 (+2.14%); the homogeneous and no-M penalties are larger at 1.514B (+2.63% and +3.20%). These results qualify any broad claim that architecture changes losses only slightly, but cover only the tested proxy configurations; see R3–R4 and R8–R11.
